sources.rationale: Six may earn a guitar-trained channel for the attacked acoustic accompaniment; two is the conservative vocals/accompaniment alternative, while four adds rhythm-section channels this sparse duet does not support.

Predominantly sustained orchestral material has no lead voice, kit, electric bass, guitar, or piano utility; two is the least misleading available contract and the long-tail instruments remain in accompaniment.
Dense guitar, bass, drums, and vocals require at least the rhythm-section split; six is useful only when pitched attacks are supported.
Real piano and a rhythm section make two tracks too coarse; four or six may be defensible after listening review.
The audible bass and drums require a rhythm-section split even though sustained reeds can resemble voice-like material.

Four may expose rap, programmed percussion, and synth bass; two remains an honest vocals/instrumental fallback, while six must not claim guitar/piano utility merely because a synthesized attack is pitched.
Upright bass and several attacked string instruments justify four or six without pretending their labels are Demucs stem names.

Four may preserve programmed drums and synth bass; two is an honest vocals/instrumental fallback, while six must not turn synthesizer attacks into an unsupported promise of useful guitar or piano channels.
This second all-MT-32 arrangement must not convert harmonic synthesizer attacks into a claim that guitar- or piano-trained channels will be useful.
Programmed rhythm and synth bass can justify four, while two remains conservative; six is rejected because the arrangement provides no verified guitar or piano evidence.
The independent house/electro control should retain rhythm-section utility without treating generic synthesized pitches as evidence for guitar and piano output.
